claim: GPT-4 exhibits significant performance collapse when using self-critique (LLM verifying and critiquing its own answers) across Game of 24, Graph Coloring, and STRIPS/Blocksworld planning, while performance gains occur only with sound external verification.
stance_target: the target paper's thesis that iterative self-generated feedback degrades LLM proposal quality without external verification
scope_conditions: GPT-4, three formally verifiable reasoning/planning domains, up to 15 rounds of iterative prompting
quoted_support: We observe significant performance collapse with self-critique and significant performance gains with sound external verification.

claim: Compounding errors in GPT-4's verification (false positives/negatives) and critique generation (misleading feedback) make the full self-critique loop perform worse than simply taking the model's first, un-iterated guess.
stance_target: iterative feedback degrading rather than improving LLM output quality
scope_conditions: GPT-4 on Game of 24, Graph Coloring, STRIPS planning
quoted_support: these errors actually reduce the performance of the LLM-based self-critique loop below that of just taking the LLM's very first guess.

claim: The CRITIC framework (Gou et al. 2023) was, per this paper's own related-work review, the first to notice that LLM self-critique can in some cases lead to decreases in performance compared to sound verification -- establishing a documented priority chain for 'self-refinement can hurt' findings predating 2024.
stance_target: novelty/priority of the claim that LLM self-refinement can degrade rather than improve outputs
quoted_support: The authors of the CRITIC framework gou2023critic were the first to notice that, in some cases, LLM self-critique can lead to decreases in performance when compared to sound verification.

claim: The best-performing configuration found is not self-critique at all but repeated sampling combined with a sound external verifier that simply selects a correct guess from among many -- i.e., the mechanism for improvement is verification/selection, not feedback-driven refinement.
stance_target: the distinction between expected-best-of-k selection under a fixed budget and iterative self-improvement as the correct estimand/mechanism for search-like LLM tasks
scope_conditions: GPT-4, three domains, sound external verifiers (VAL for planning, expression simplification for Game of 24, constraint checker for graph coloring)
quoted_support: We also found that good performance can be achieved without any critique whatsoever: just let the LLM make many guesses, and have a sound verifier pick any that is actually correct.

claim: This paper explicitly contradicts prior optimistic claims about LLM self-reflection, including Reflexion's claim of an 'emergent property of self-reflection in LLMs' and Self-Refine's claim that LLMs can often provide useful feedback and improve their own output without human input.
stance_target: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) and Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023) claims that LLM self-reflection/self-refinement reliably improves outputs
quoted_support: Our results contradict earlier work that has been very optimistic about LLM self-critique abilities.

claim: The paper cites FunSearch and the LLM-Modulo framework as real-world architectures that have already shown success by pairing LLM generation with external sound verification/critics rather than relying on intrinsic self-critique.
stance_target: what architectures actually work when combining LLMs with iterative search/feedback
quoted_support: In real-world applications we expect this role to be played by a menagerie of partial critics evaluating plans or solutions based on criteria that they have access to, designed so that consensus is considered verification. Similar architectures have already shown some success funsearch, and previous work has proposed the general LLM-Modulo framework kambhampati2024llms which the current work fits into.
